//: Store-readiness policy the expo-policy gate enforces over the RESOLVED config — the review-rejection surface as reviewable data. Every value here is a reviewed human decision (the file is write-guard-protected). androidTargetSdk: `floor` is Google Play's rolling target-API requirement, and it is a DATED one — from 2026-08-31 new apps AND app updates must target Android 16 (API 36) or higher to be submitted at all, so the floor moved 35 -> 36 in harness 0.5.0 (reviewed 2026-08-06, 25 days ahead of the deadline; an extension to 2026-11-01 is requestable in the Play Console but is a per-developer act this file cannot assume). Wear OS / Automotive stay at 35 and TV / XR at 34 — a project shipping one of those form factors lowers this floor deliberately, in a reviewed commit, which is what this file being reviewed data is for. SOURCE: https://developer.android.com/google/play/requirements/target-sdk. expoSdkDefaults maps an Expo SDK major to the targetSdkVersion it ships when the config declares none (SDK 57 targets 36, so a stock scaffold already satisfies the raised floor and only a config that pinned 35 by hand goes red) — an UNKNOWN SDK major fails closed until a human pins it. iosEncryption: nonExemptAllowed=true (with a reason) is the reviewed escape for apps that genuinely ship non-exempt cryptography; the gate requires ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption to be DECLARED either way. usageDescriptionKeysByPlugin: which InfoPlist purpose strings a config plugin implies — the pre-prebuild surface (a bare npm dep without a plugin is invisible until prebuild; Apple's post-submission validation remains the backstop). trackingSdkSignals: plugin/dependency names that mean the app tracks — with none present, an ATT string or NSPrivacyTracking declaration is an unreviewed tracking claim and reds; with one present, all three declarations must agree. privacyAccessedApiTypes: the reviewed lockstep for ios.privacyManifests NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes rows ({ category, reasons, why }) — declared-but-unreviewed and reviewed-but-undeclared both red. accountDeletion: the Apple 5.1.1(v) closure — surface 'action' asserts the command-registry id + the backing Edge Function (edgeFunction: its supabase/functions/<name>/index.ts exists AND config.toml declares [functions.<name>]) exist whenever an auth surface ships; 'route' asserts a ROUTES id + the Edge Function; 'external' (https url + reason) and 'none' (reason) are the reviewed escapes. icons.solidColorPlaceholder: 'warn' keeps the scaffold's deliberate placeholder art green with a NOTE; flip to 'error' as a pre-submission step.
